messages:
Sam: hey everyone, started today! Trying to follow the quickstart but `kubectl config get-contexts` shows a dozen contexts and `kubectl get pods -n onboarding` gives Forbidden. Who do I ask to get proper namespace access?
Nina (eng-infra): welcome Sam :wave: we handle that. First, what's `kubectl config current-context` and are you using AWS SSO or local kubeconfig?
Sam: current-context is `rwd-us-central` and I'm using SSO via the browser. SSO login seemed fine but I still can't access onboarding ns.
access-bot: ticket INFRA-2620 created for Sam (sam@redwood.com). Assigned: Nina. SLA: 2h.
Nina (eng-infra): sounds like your directory groups haven't synced to our RBAC yet. Two short options: (A) we add a RoleBinding for your group in `onboarding` or (B) create a temporary serviceaccount token so you can run the labs immediately. Which do you prefer?
Sam: need quick access for the lab. Token ok. Also curious if there's a safer way to avoid mixing up contexts across terminals.
Nina (eng-infra): for quick access run:```bash
kubectl -n onboarding create serviceaccount sam-onboard || true
TOKEN=$(kubectl -n onboarding create token sam-onboard --duration=6h)
kubectl config set-credentials sam-onboard --token="$TOKEN"
kubectl config set-context sam-onboarding --cluster=rwd-dev-cluster --namespace=onboarding --user=sam-onboard
kubectl config use-context sam-onboarding
```This creates a dedicated context for the exercise. To avoid context mixups: either export KUBECONFIG per shell or use `kubectl config rename-context` to add a clear prefix like `>>>` for prod.
Omar: another tip: we keep a per-user kubeconfig directory `~/.kube/<user>` and a tiny shell helper `kctx` to switch and show a big red warning if the context contains `prod`. Ping me and I'll add you to the helper.
Sam: token created and `kubectl get pods -n onboarding` works now, thanks!
Priya: FYI the SSO group sync sometimes lags ~10-15m after directory changes; if Nina adds you to the `developers` group you may need to `logout` from SSO then `login` again.
Nina (eng-infra): I've also opened a proper RoleBinding for `group:developers` in onboarding so the token is temporary. You should see the group reflected after your next SSO reauth. I'll close INFRA-2620 once you confirm.
Sam: confirmed I can access with the token and after re-login my SSO group shows `developers` and I can `kubectl` without the temp context. Big thanks, and excited to be here! :smile:
Nina (eng-infra): welcome aboard Sam. If you want help installing the `kube-helpers` scripts or the prod-warning plugin DM me.
